expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionBase & (status variants) with discriminant on status literal

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each union member carries only fields relevant to its status

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: assertNever function used in hasAccess switch with default case

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionId, CustomerId, PlanId as branded types

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Provides only a type definition stub (LegalTransitions) with empty arrays; states 'nothing stops canceled → trialing'; no actual transition function or runtime constraint

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Enumerates 5 misuses: optional-fields combinatorial explosion, silent undefined comparison, boolean independence, silent fallthrough, string ID swaps

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is discriminated union; explicitly contrasts with problematic approach
